verdicts.quote: without any further action by anyone, the waiting member who is first in line (and still allowed, see C-27) is booked into the class
the one who joined earliest is the first to receive a free place. Nobody is moved ahead of an earlier joiner for any reason (for example membership type or how often they book).
A member may be on the waitlists of several classes at once, each with its own position; joining, leaving or being booked from one does not change their position on another.
verdicts.missing: What happens to the waitlist entry (or a later promotion) for a class overlapping in time with one the member was just booked into.

verdicts.quote: After a booked member cancels, or staff remove a booked member, and at least one member is waiting for that class, then without any further action by anyone, the waiting member who is first in line ... is booked
verdicts.missing: How promptly the background promotion must happen after the triggering cancellation.

verdicts.quote: the next time they open their classes the new booking is there ... If the app sends a confirmation to members when they book a class, a member booked from the waitlist receives that same kind of confirmation.
verdicts.missing: A definite channel and message content, and what happens when sending the notification fails.

verdicts.quote: When k places are freed, no more than k members are booked from the waitlist, no member is booked into the same class twice
no member is booked into the same class twice, and each member who is booked is no longer shown as waiting.
used up at the moment the member is booked from the waitlist, and not before. / would be refused a booking for any reason ... they are not booked and the next member in line is considered
There is no fixed limit on how many members can wait for a class ... with 500 waiting, the next member can join and is told position 501.
From the moment a class has started (or earlier, at the time after which the app already refuses new bookings, if it has such a time), a place that frees up is not given to a waiting member
When staff raise the capacity of a class by k places and at least k members are eligible and waiting, the first k eligible waiting members, in order, are booked.
verdicts.missing: What happens when staff lower a class's capacity while a waitlist exists (and to existing bookings above the new capacity).

verdicts.quote: After staff cancel a class, no member appears as waiting for it and no one is booked into it from the waitlist; the waiting members see the class as cancelled, as booked members do.
Positions are whole numbers counting from 1 in order of joining
verdicts.missing: The waitlist entry as a record (join time, state such as waiting/promoted/removed/skipped) and whether position is stored or derived from join order.

verdicts.quote: members still waiting are not booked, and no longer appear as waiting.
verdicts.missing: What becomes of the entries once the class has run (deleted, archived, marked expired) and how long they are retained.

verdicts.quote: A member's view of a waitlist shows their own position and no other member's name or contact details.
Wherever staff can see who is booked into a class, they can also see the members waiting for it, in position order, marked as waiting and not as booked.
verdicts.missing: Whether staff can manually promote or remove a waiting member, and a record of who was promoted when.

verdicts.quote: The new version starts and offers the waitlist with no new setting
verdicts.missing: No way to turn the feature off or enable it per class or class type is provided; only reverting to the previous version.

verdicts.quote: A member who is allowed to book a class with at least one free place is booked as they are today, with the same result and the same rules applied.
every existing class, booking and member is present and unchanged, the booked members of every class are the same, and every class has an empty waitlist.
